daily.full:
Consensus

The clearest common bullish name today was $LITE: 4 accounts explicitly bullish across 23 related posts. @kevinxu said he hopes someone dreamed of photonics — a full position in calls would be legendary. Post @aleabitoreddit reported that $MRVL is in the final stage of acquiring $LITE, aiming to ease supply bottlenecks through laser vertical integration; if it goes through, other laser makers could be re-rated. Post @StockSavvyShay highlighted $MRVL profit growing nearly 10x to about $14B by FY2029, hoping to benefit as hyperscalers keep raising AI spend.

Common bearish

$INTC had 3 bearish accounts. @hkuppy said don't forget 2000 — the semiconductor mania ended when Intel blew up; shares sank after hours on a sharply lower Q4 guide (adjusted EPS $0.25 vs $0.43 expected). Post @munster_gene said the main issue is PC demand slowing on high memory costs, and it should not be extrapolated to $NVDA.

Split

$GOOGL was the most-mentioned ticker today (66 mentions), with clearly divided views. @Mr_Derivatives noted that despite a 10% drop, every major analyst still has big targets of $375–425, 30–47% above the current price — buy the dip? Post Meanwhile @TheTranscript_ reported Alphabet's CEO saying AI tools help engineers ship 35% more code with 30% fewer bugs. Post Some see strong fundamentals; others worry about after-hours weakness dragging the market.

Also worth noting

Small caps in $IWM were relatively strong; @Mr_Derivatives said it almost touched $283 after hours after a decent rebound over the past week. Post $CVNA beat estimates with retail units +39% to a record, up 8% after hours; @michaelsikand mentioned an $1.8B hedge fund manager with 80% of capital long. Post On $MU, one account sees a possible $1,700 within 18 months, saying bears will be proven wrong again as free-cash-flow estimates have been raised sharply.

Consensus

Clearest common bullish today is $NVDA, with 4 accounts long and 13 related posts. @Beth_Kindig estimates Nvidia ACIE revenue growth may outpace hyperscalers (138.5% vs 101.2%) and could catch up in about five to six quarters. post @Jason said he bought some $GOOG and $NVDA, citing strong leadership and products. post @StockSavvyShay noted reports that $NVDA is in talks to provide over $5B of credit support for a 460MW Nscale data center backed by a $45B $ANT compute contract. post On rotation, @KeithMcCullough said Hedgeye put its highest equity allocation into healthcare $XLV, with the community also re-adding staples $XLP.

Common Bearish

$RDDT has 10 bearish accounts, the densest common short today, with 24 related posts. @ripster47 called it a major disappointment after daily active users missed, saying longs were covered around $135 and framing a 100 PSYCH short setup. post @StockSavvyShay listed $RDDT among October growth-stock drawdowns (about -41%). post $INTC has 9 bearish accounts and 48 posts: @TrendSpider said it was down about 30% from the prior close, the worst drop in the company's 55-year history; @garyblack00 pointed to soft PC demand outlook and guidance as accelerating tech outflows. post post Several also flagged $NOW wiping out three months of gains and breaking the 200-day average.

Divergence

$AMZN is among the most-mentioned names, with 5 bullish and 2 bearish accounts and 66 posts. @munster_gene argued AWS growth supports a new narrative, with AWS about 25% of sales today and maybe at least half of revenue in five years; @ChrisCamillo said he aggressively added $AMZN while de-levering elsewhere, viewing the market as too dangerous for short-term over-trading; @saxena_puru noted the post-print drop but said AI buildout is not slowing, with Alphabet maintaining $195-205B 2026 capex guidance. post post post $SNDK is similarly split (3 long / 4 short): some cite the Sandisk CEO saying AI infrastructure customers underestimated NAND demand, while others still list it among post-earnings tech declines.

Other Notable

@RedDogT3 noted that at least $TSLA offers a layered system to navigate, holding $387-$388 to add and manage. post @OptionsMike is watching the $SPY 748.80 level. On the drone/defense theme, @ripster47 and @TrendSpider mentioned names like $ONDS warming up. Overall, post-earnings stock differentiation exceeds any single index narrative.

$AAPL has 4 bullish accounts. @charliebilello said Apple is now the only Magnificent 7 stock outperforming the S&P 500 this year because it generates more free cash flow than any other Mag 7 company while largely avoiding the capex consuming its hyperscale peers. post @bespokeinvest noted large tech divergence, with $AAPL and $MSFT the only two in uptrends. post @JC_ParetsX mentioned decent buying on dips. post

$GOOGL 1 long 1 short, 17 posts. @TheTranscript_ quoted Alphabet CEO: Google processes 32 billion AI tokens per minute, up over 4x year-over-year, first-party model API near 32 billion tokens per minute, up 40% from last quarter and over 4x from a year ago. post But @OptionsMike said earnings were terrible, moat eroding, ads/search/YouTube missed, next year capex up sharply and FCF negative, perhaps 273 can hold, watching dead cat bounce. post

$TSLA 2 long 1 short. @OptionsMike said Friday action was firm, closed above 8-day and all MAs, watching 410 on bounce, relatively strong. post @TrendSpider said Tesla finally broke its 2026 downtrend. post But @garyblack00 worries EV market share has steadily fallen from 80% to 52%, who gained share? Math requires 100%, so others must have taken share. post

$MSFT 3 long 1 short. @OptionsMike said earnings strong and the only hyperscaler with positive cash flow, but then announced at least $25B bond issuance, sees it as preferred on bounce, watching 50-day. post @Mr_Derivatives said earlier this year he was fully bullish on MSFT, calling it a beautiful bottom. post

$SPY 2 long 1 short. @Stephanie_Link noted October stats: SPX down 93 bps but 9 of 11 sectors up, stocks above 50-day rose from 20% to 61%. post @OddStats mentioned YTD +10.7%, historically only 3 times negative for the rest of the year after such gains. post But one account noted this is the 9th time in 40 years the S&P 500 had at least 6 negative calendar months by end of October.

Other Notable

Crypto-related $COIN and $HOOD each 1 long 1 short. @TrendSpider noted for $COIN a long-only algo backtest +74% while stock down 63%; for $HOOD strategy +1,072% vs buy-and-hold +849%. But @OptionsMike is bearish due to flat earnings plus Binance hack, for $HOOD Friday low as support or else watching 73. post Overall, large tech post-earnings divergence is clear, AI narrative persists, but individual fundamentals and technical levels are the main points of disagreement.

daily.full:
Consensus

$TSLA had 6 bullish accounts and 0 bearish, across 20 related posts. @TrendSpider said an algorithm just issued the next entry signal; the strategy returned 102% vs 79% buy-and-hold, with a 58% win rate. Post. @OptionsHawk noted the stock broke recent highs with popular call options looking good. Post.

$PLTR also had 4 bullish and 0 bearish. @amitisinvesting highlighted 96% revenue growth, 62% adjusted operating margin, US commercial revenue surpassing government for the first time (+148% YoY), and 165% net dollar retention. Post. @TrendSpider also cited the beat and raised guidance. Post.

$AAPL had 4 bullish accounts. @TrendSpider reported Q4 EPS of $2.10 vs $1.98 expected, revenue $114.477B vs $113.392B. Post. @munster_gene said the better December revenue guide matters more than slightly softer margin guidance. Post.

Shared bearish

$ORCL had 3 bearish accounts. @KobeissiLetter noted the stock fell over 5% after the company announced plans to raise $20B via equity and debt for AI buildout; it is now down 54% from this year’s high. Post. @RedDogT3 called the past year or so a disaster. Post.

$CBRS also saw bearish comments, with a USB target cut from $330 to $250 and the stock falling below $100.

Splits

The $LITE–$MRVL deal was the biggest topic with 26 posts. @michaelsikand thinks the timing is bad but believes $LITE is worth far more than $1,000 a share and is not selling; the bigger takeaway is bullish for photonics overall. Post. @amitisinvesting calls the deal terrible: all-stock creates heavy dilution, closes only in 2028, and capacity is sold through 2029. Post. @garyblack00 noted the offer is about $1,132 per share, a 24% premium to the 10/28 close of $914. Post.

Other notes

$SPCX saw discussion of a possible Boost Mobile acquisition or network use tied to Elon Musk’s wireless plans. @StockSavvyShay mentioned roughly 7 million users and 5G infrastructure. Post.

Consensus

Over the past month the most concentrated common bullish names were $SOFI (8 accounts) and $LITE (5 accounts). Photonics and fintech themes held up on the longer time frame. $MSTR, $RSP and $AEHR also had 5 bullish accounts each.

Common bearish

$BA kept 4 bearish accounts, consistent with the weekly view. Other common bearish names included $TMUS, $SBUX and $ENPH.

Split

$CRWV was the most extreme split: 6 bullish accounts but 24 bearish. @KeithMcCullough said the AI bubble has started to pop, beginning with the neoclouds; CoreWeave closed at $54.24 on Oct 23, well off its 52-week high. Post On the other side, one account noted that even $GOOGL can't bring capacity online fast enough to meet demand, which helps names like $CRWV. $TSLA had 22 bullish and 3 bearish accounts; $SPY was 12 bullish vs 13 bearish.

Also worth noting

Overall, AI-related splits (especially neoclouds and semiconductors) were most visible on the monthly view, while traditional defensive and consumer names drew few common bullish calls.

briefings.html:
Today's market snapshot

324 posts from 66 accounts, 157 bullish vs 51 bearish. The most aligned common bullish name was $TSLA, after the CFO cited the highest vehicle backlog in four years. Common bearish centred on $BA, which fell sharply after a wider loss and a cut to delivery guidance. $SOFI beat estimates and some see it above $35. $NVDA and $SPY were split. Not investment advice.

Today's market highlights

Over the past ~25 hours, 52 accounts posted 305 related items. Consensus centred on the photonics theme in $LITE, with 4 accounts explicitly bullish on $MRVL acquisition talk and AI connectivity demand. Common bearish focused on the reaction to $INTC's sharply lower guidance. The biggest split was $GOOGL: after a 10% drop, analyst targets remain at $375–425. Small caps in $IWM almost touched $283, and $CVNA beat estimates, +8% after hours. AI-related names reacted unevenly overall; watch for stock-level divergence after the FOMC.

Today's market highlights

Over the past ~27 hours, 58 accounts posted 320 related items. Common bearish is led by $RDDT (10 accounts), with daily active users missing triggering cover and short-setup discussion; @ripster47 mentioned covering around $135. $INTC also has 9 bearish accounts, with some noting about a 30% drop from the prior close. Common bullish includes $NVDA with 4 accounts long. Biggest splits are on $AMZN (5 long / 2 short) and $SNDK (3/4): one side emphasizes AWS/NAND and AI infrastructure demand, the other focuses on the post-earnings selloff. @RedDogT3 is watching the $TSLA $387-388 layered management zone. Weekly common bearish is also led by $RDDT.

Today's Market Highlights

Over the past ~25.5 hours, 65 accounts posted 213 related items. Common bullish is led by $MSFT (4 accounts), with @TrendSpider saying Azure is accelerating and @TheTranscript_ noting cloud backlog surging to about $1.8T; $AAPL has 2 bullish accounts, with @TrendSpider setting a $400 target. No pure common bearish, but $INTC is clearly split (1 long / 6 short), with @Mr_Derivatives noting record daily selling volume. Most-mentioned are $AMZN and $NVDA, with mixed views; AI narrative still dominates, but individual stock differentiation outweighs any single index direction. Weekly common bearish is also led by $RDDT (11 accounts).
